proof_skeleton_nl: First split off the branch where the generated ideal is the whole ring; that exceptional case is isolated as an explicit bottleneck. In the proper-ideal branch, finite-dimensionality implies the ideal is m-primary, so after localizing at m=(x_1,...,x_d) the quotient has finite length. Properness plus homogeneity also forces every generator to lie in m. The local ring S_m is regular local of dimension d, so the localized sequence g_1/1,...,g_d/1 is regular by the regular-local criterion. Localization-quotient compatibility then identifies the localized successive quotients, and a graded local-to-global injectivity lemma descends injectivity from each localized quotient back to the original graded quotient. Finally combine the two branches and rewrite the result as the statement that g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence.

steps.derives: Let I=(g_1,...,g_d). Then either I=S or I is a proper ideal of S.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the basic dichotomy between the unit ideal and a proper ideal.

steps.derives: In the case I=S, for every i with 1 <= i <= d, the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the direct content of L1.

steps.derives: In the case I is proper, the localized quotient S_m / I S_m has finite length as an S_m-module.
steps.trivial_justification: Under the proper-ideal branch, I is a proper homogeneous ideal because the generators g_1,...,g_d are homogeneous. The root hypothesis gives that S/I is finite-dimensional over k. Applying L2 yields m^N subseteq I for some N, and hence after localizing at m the quotient S_m/IS_m is a finite-length S_m-module.

steps.derives: In the case I is proper, each generator g_i belongs to m, and therefore each localized element g_i/1 belongs to m S_m.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L3 to the proper homogeneous ideal I=(g_1,...,g_d). Since localization sends m into mS_m, each g_i/1 lies in the maximal ideal of S_m.

steps.derives: The localization S_m is a regular local ring of Krull dimension d with maximal ideal m S_m.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the assertion of L4.

steps.derives: In the case I is proper, for every i with 1 <= i <= d, the image of g_i/1 in S_m / (g_1,...,g_{i-1}) S_m is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L5 to the regular local ring R=S_m from Step A5 and to the sequence a_j=g_j/1. Step A4 gives a_j in mS_m for every j, and Step A3 gives that R/(a_1,...,a_d)=S_m/IS_m has finite length. Therefore L5 yields that for each i, multiplication by g_i/1 is injective on S_m/(g_1,...,g_{i-1})S_m.

steps.derives: In the case I is proper, for every i with 1 <= i <= d, multiplication by g_i on the localized module (S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}))_m is injective.
steps.trivial_justification: Fix i and set I_{i-1}=(g_1,...,g_{i-1}). Lemma L6 with R=S, U the complement of m, h=g_i, and I=I_{i-1} identifies (S/I_{i-1})_m with S_m/I_{i-1}S_m and identifies the localized multiplication-by-g_i map with multiplication by g_i/1 on S_m/I_{i-1}S_m. Step A6 says the latter map is injective, so the former localized map is injective.

steps.derives: For every i with 1 <= i <= d, the quotient M_i := S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is a finitely generated graded S-module, and g_i is a homogeneous element of S.
steps.trivial_justification: Each ideal (g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is homogeneous because its generators are homogeneous, so the quotient M_i inherits a grading. As a quotient of the Noetherian ring S, each M_i is finitely generated. Homogeneity of g_i is part of the theorem hypothesis.

steps.derives: In the case I is proper, for every i with 1 <= i <= d, the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: Fix i and let M_i=S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}). Step A8 gives that M_i is a finitely generated graded S-module and that g_i is homogeneous. Step A7 gives injectivity of multiplication by g_i on (M_i)_m. Applying L7 to M_i and g_i yields injectivity of multiplication by g_i on M_i itself. Since i was arbitrary, the non-zero-divisor statement holds for every i.

steps.derives: Without any extra case assumption, for every i with 1 <= i <= d, the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: By Step A1 there are only two cases. If I=S, Step A2 gives the desired conclusion. If I is proper, Step A9 gives the same conclusion. Therefore the conclusion holds unconditionally.

steps.derives: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. If g_1,...,g_d are homogeneous elements of S and S/(g_1,...,g_d) is finite-dimensional over k, then for each i the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence.
steps.trivial_justification: Step A10 gives the successive non-zero-divisor statement. Because the g_i are homogeneous, L8 identifies that statement exactly with the assertion that g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence.
